title: Gap map — 1:1 brief (Zoe Chen)
content:
Purpose and constraints:
- 20 minute async-friendly 1:1. High-signal, lightweight. Goal: identify the single highest-impact gap for next sprint and concrete micro-actions.
- Keep it coach-first: ask, reflect, then suggest.
- Avoid diving into infra debugging during this slot; park technical triage to a follow-up.

Context (notes to self):
- Report: Malik Rao (senior engineer, serving-runtime). Recently rotated to KV cache work. Has taken on ownership of cache eviction policy but hasn't shipped config rollout yet.
- Signals: slower than expected rollout velocity, a couple of regression alerts last week (p99 latency blips), volunteered for mentorship program.
- Org priority alignment: Q3 OKR A.2 (reduce tail latency for small-model workloads). This 1:1 should connect Malik's work to that OKR and make the next step measurable.

Top-line meeting agenda (20m):
1) Quick personal check-in (2m): energy level + one non-work highlight.
2) Signal readout (3m): ask Malik to surface 1 metric or event that mattered since last 1:1.
3) Gap identification (7m): discuss what’s actually blocking the rollout and why progress slowed. Use the gap-map prompts below.
4) Micro-action mapping (6m): turn gap into 1–3 concrete actions with owners and dates.
5) Close & alignment (2m): confirm next touchpoint and what I will unblock before then.

Gap-map prompts (for probing):
- \"What would you do tomorrow if nothing blocked you?\" (forces concrete endpoint)
- \"What's the smallest validation we can run to know this is working end-to-end?\"
- \"Which dependency, if removed, would double your throughput?\"
- \"Is the blocker people (review bandwidth), infra (capacity), or product (spec uncertainty)?\"

Possible hypotheses for Malik's slowdown (to test quickly):
- Review queue: two key PRs are blocked on one overbooked reviewer (SRE).
- Performance regression uncertainty: lack of a small canonical benchmark confuses rollout gating.
- Cross-team coordination: private-deployments team needs an interface tweak.

Micro-action map (example outputs we want from the meeting):
- Action A: Create a 1-page rollout checklist and a smoke benchmark (owner: Malik) — deliverable: checklist + benchmark script in repo by 2027-07-19.
- Action B: I (Zoe) will ping SRE lead and add reviewer capacity for two days (owner: Zoe) — ETA: 2027-07-14.
- Action C: If interface tweak is required, open lean RFC called \"cache-evict-shim\" and tag private-deployments (owner: Malik) — ETA: 2027-07-16.
- Action D (backup): If smoke benchmark shows p99 issues, schedule 30m deep-dive with perf folks and Malik (owner: Zoe + Malik) — contingency window 2027-07-20 to 2027-07-22.

Signals to track (post-meeting):
- CI: benchmark CI runs pass and baseline number published (artifact link).
- PR velocity: blocked PRs reduced from 2 -> 0 within 1 week.
- Latency signal: p99 tail for small-model workload improved <=10% of baseline by end of next sprint.

Notes-to-self: coaching cues and language
- Use \"Tell me the last time this worked\" to surface concrete steps and avoid hypotheticals.
- Mirror ownership language: name the owner when agreeing actions (\"You’ll own the checklist, I’ll own the reviewer ask\").
- If Malik shrugs on deadlines, offer a trade-off: \"Would you rather ship a narrower checklist sooner or a fuller rollout later?\"

Meeting script (short):
- Start: \"How's the week? One win and one thing that sucked.\"
- Transition: \"Give me a single signal that mattered since last time — metric, regression, or blocker.\"
- Drill: \"If that signal is real, what's the smallest test that proves the fix?\"
- Close: \"Ok, clear. We'll do A/B/C — I'll follow up on B by Friday and you'll drop the checklist by next Tuesday. I'll block time for the reviewer if needed.\"

Follow-up template to send after meeting (quick DM/email):
- Subject: Quick recap — Malik 1:1 (2027-07-13)
- Body bullets: 1) What we agreed; 2) Actions with owners + dates; 3) What I'll unblock; 4) Ask for confirmation if anything missing.

Personal reminders (private):
- After the meeting, immediately add the three actions to my calendar and set a 3-day reminder to ping SRE.
- Add smoke benchmark CI job to tracking board (project: serving-runtime/perf).
- Keep this 1:1 light — avoid getting pulled into implementation details; escalate to a follow-up working session if needed.

Loose questions to consider in the follow-up working session (if triggered):
- Can we simulate KV cache evictions deterministically in staging?
- Do we need a canary routing policy to test config safely?
- Is there a low-effort quantization or sequence-length cap that would neutralize the p99 blips?

End-state success (how I’ll rate this 1:1 as productive):
- Malik leaves with 2 clear deliverables and dates.
- I have committed unblock actions (reviewer ask) and calendar blocks.
- Within one week, concrete artifacts (checklist + smoke benchmark) exist and at least one blocked PR has moved forward.

Quick log (to fill after meeting):
- Time started:
- Time ended:
- Main signal Malik raised:
- Agreed actions: (copy/paste micro-action map with owners/dates)
- My immediate follow-ups (checkboxes): [ ] ping SRE lead; [ ] add calendar blockers; [ ] create CI tracking card

End of brief.

(Extra: keep this file as a local scratch — move final action list into the team tracker if outcomes are validated.)
